head: be87ad5721901f90b507bb9f8b3ba5f9454295b0
scope: Current uncommitted application diff, including the performance changes and existing employee-editing / AI-exclusion work; deployment dependencies and migration state also checked.

findings.severity: high dependency advisory; authenticated application exposure
findings.problem: Installed Zod 3.25.76 validates every element of oversized constrained arrays before rejecting their length. jsonBody parses the full request, and apiError formats every validation issue. The board no-answer route authenticates first, but an authenticated caller can submit an oversized array despite the 50-item schema limit.

evidence.method: Bounded local execution of the route schema and API issue formatting, using installed Zod and a 256 MiB Node heap limit. No HTTP request, database mutation, or attempt to exhaust memory.

findings.limitations: Demonstrates unbounded per-element validation and error amplification, not a server crash. Production ingress limits and rate limits were not established. Authentication reduces exposure compared with the generic advisory.
findings.requiredBeforeApproval: Resolve the advisory with a compatible patched dependency or enforce request and collection limits before schema validation, bound returned validation errors, and verify deployed limits with targeted tests. Do not blindly apply major dependency upgrades.

findings.problem: Initial page rendering waits for a separate physical-row fingerprint before reading batch data. This adds a table-scanning query to the critical path and offsets the member-query improvements. AI detail reads were slower in every measured pair.

evidence.method: Before and after reader sequences on the same pinned PostgreSQL connection in one enforced REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot; alternating execution order across three pairs. Before is the pre-optimization working-tree snapshot. After includes batchVersion plus the new batch readers. All 24 samples across four paths returned equivalent results.

findings.limitations: A small sample against the largest existing AI batch, not end-to-end browser or concurrent load testing. Excludes unchanged authentication, user lookups and rendering. Other batch paths showed mixed cache-sensitive results; this finding does not claim every page is slower.
findings.requiredBeforeApproval: Remove the separate expensive fingerprint from the initial critical path, for example by deriving a cheap token from the same authoritative read or maintaining inexpensive change metadata. Preserve the rule that a token must not acknowledge data absent from the rendered snapshot. Repeat paired page-sequence measurements and invalidation / draft-preservation tests.

dependencyAudit.highPackageExplanation: OpenAI is flagged through Zod; these are not two independent high-severity vulnerabilities.
dependencyAudit.nextAdvisories: Seven moderate advisories reported; fixes are available. Inspected application code did not show the documented use-cache, Cache Components, Edge runtime, image optimization or transparent fetched-response forwarding preconditions. Exploitability was not demonstrated.

migrationReview.method: Read-only comparison of local migration SHA-256 checksums against the configured database migration ledger.
migrationReview.notes: The additional historical ledger entry and retained-schema trigger configuration are preserved. No migration or trigger changes were performed.

validation.note: These are prior results for the unchanged source, not newly repeated full test suites. This review added paired read-only performance/parity measurements, migration verification, a fresh production dependency audit and the bounded validation reproduction.

limits: Passing functional tests does not establish production latency or eliminate all concurrency risks.
No live provider mutation, production load test, deployment, commit or push was performed during this review.
Release approval remains withheld until the listed findings are resolved and the changed paths revalidated.
